<button onclick="window.print()" style="float:right;margin-bottom:1rem">🖨 Print / Save as PDF</button>

::: {.callout-note}
## Overview
CitraPrep isolates intact nuclei from snap-frozen tissue for downstream single-nucleus work (Step 15: "Load for single cell"). Tissue is dounce-homogenized in a citrate-based homogenization buffer (CitraHB), then nuclei are purified on an iodixanol step gradient in an **ultracentrifuge** (18 min scheduled run time, ~1 hr total with load/accel/no-brake coast, 10,000×g, **no brake**) and collected from the gradient interface. RNase inhibitors (SUPERase•In™ RNase Inhibitor + RNasin® Ribonuclease Inhibitor) go into every buffer **except** the final nuclei resuspension buffer — spermine, spermidine, and dithiothreitol (DTT) are deliberately left out of that one because they interfere with downstream cDNA synthesis.

<!-- TODO: confirm original source/citation for this protocol with JP — none given in the source document -->
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## Before starting
- Use **cell culture grade water** for every "water" call in this protocol (stock buffers and 1000X fresh solutions alike) — not general lab ddH₂O.
- Make 1 M Tricine–Potassium Hydroxide (Tricine-KOH, pH 7.8) and 1 M Citric Acid stocks first — CitraHB and Diluent are both built from them.
- Prepare CitraHB, Diluent, and Detergent stock buffers **a day ahead** — good for 1 month at 4°C.
- Pre-chill the 7 mL glass dounce homogenizer on ice.
- Make 1 M Dithiothreitol (DTT), 0.15 M spermine, and 0.5 M spermidine (1000X stocks) **fresh** each time.
- Make CitraHB Complete (stock + protease inhibitor tablet) fresh; add spermine/spermidine/DTT to bring it to 1X.
- Make the nuclei resuspension buffer during the centrifugation step (Step 8) — **no** spermine, spermidine, or DTT in this one.
- Set the **ultracentrifuge** to 4°C and confirm the rotor/tubes are rated for **no-brake** deceleration (Step 8).
- Book more time than the spin itself: the 18 min is only the run — loading, vacuum draw-down, acceleration, and the unbraked coast to a stop routinely bring the whole ultracentrifuge step to **around an hour**. Schedule accordingly.
:::

## Configure experiment

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof n_samples  = Inputs.number({label: "Number of samples", value: 1, min: 1, max: 24, step: 1})
viewof excess_pct = Inputs.number({label: "Extra overage on scaled solutions (%)", value: 0, min: 0, max: 30, step: 5})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
scale = n_samples * (1 + excess_pct / 100)
fmt   = (x, d = 2) => x.toFixed(d)

md`**${n_samples} sample(s) · ${excess_pct}% overage · scale factor ${fmt(scale)}×**`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// RNase inhibitor target/stock — single source of truth for every buffer below.
// This protocol uses 0.5 U/µL final for BOTH SUPERase and RNAsin (not 0.2 U/µL).
rnase_final = 0.5   // U/µL, final concentration of each inhibitor
rnase_stock = 40    // U/µL, assumed stock concentration — edit if yours differs
rnase_vol   = (V) => rnase_final * V / rnase_stock   // volume of stock needed for total volume V (same units as V)
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Ordering quantities (from source protocol)
Per sample, the original protocol notes you will need roughly **1 mL SUPERase** and **500 µL Protector** (RNase inhibitor) on hand for ordering purposes. The line-item breakdown below is the granular per-buffer calculation — it will not sum to exactly this figure, since the source note is a rough ordering estimate rather than a derived total.

## Stock buffers

Make ~1 month's supply at once; store at 4°C. These do **not** scale with sample count — they're a standing stock, not a per-run master mix.

### 1 M stock reagents (make first)

CitraHB and Diluent both draw their Tricine-KOH and Citric Acid components from 1 M stocks. Pick a batch volume and the amounts scale automatically.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof stock_vol_mL = Inputs.number({label: "1M stock batch volume (mL)", value: 100, min: 10, step: 10})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
tricine_MW = 179.17
citric_MW  = 192.124

tricine_g = 1 * (stock_vol_mL / 1000) * tricine_MW
citric_g  = 1 * (stock_vol_mL / 1000) * citric_MW

Inputs.table([
  {Component: "Tricine (free acid)", "Amount": `${fmt(tricine_g)} g`, "Recipe": `Dissolve in ~80% of ${fmt(stock_vol_mL)} mL cell culture grade water; titrate to pH 7.8 with Potassium Hydroxide (KOH); bring to ${fmt(stock_vol_mL)} mL`},
  {Component: "Citric Acid",         "Amount": `${fmt(citric_g)} g`,  "Recipe": `Dissolve in cell culture grade water to ${fmt(stock_vol_mL)} mL`}
], {layout: "auto"})
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Why Tricine needs KOH and citric acid doesn't
Tricine-KOH is the free-acid form of Tricine titrated to pH 7.8 with Potassium Hydroxide (KOH) — the "-KOH" in the name refers to this titration, not a separate reagent added at the bench. Citric Acid stock is used as-is; both CitraHB and Diluent get their acidic character partly from it, so no pH adjustment is needed here.
:::

**CitraHB (30 mL)**

| Component | Final conc. | Amount |
|-----------|-------------|--------|
| Sucrose | 0.25 M | 2.567 g |
| Potassium Chloride (KCl) | 25 mM | 55.9 mg |
| Magnesium Chloride (MgCl₂) | 5 mM | 14.3 mg |
| Tricine-KOH pH 7.8 | 20 mM | 600 µL of 1 M stock |
| Citric Acid | 10 mM | 300 µL of 1 M stock |

Dissolve in cell culture grade water to a final volume of 30 mL.

**Diluent (10 mL)**

| Component | Final conc. | Amount |
|-----------|-------------|--------|
| Potassium Chloride (KCl) | 150 mM | 111.8 mg |
| Magnesium Chloride (MgCl₂) | 30 mM | 28.6 mg |
| Tricine-KOH pH 7.8 | 120 mM | 1.2 mL of 1 M stock |
| Citric Acid | 10 mM | 100 µL of 1 M stock |

Dissolve in cell culture grade water to a final volume of 10 mL.

**Detergent (1 mL)**

| Component | Amount |
|-----------|--------|
| IGEPAL CA-630 | 50 µL |
| CitraHB | 950 µL |

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Buffer storage
CitraHB, Diluent, and Detergent are stable at 4°C for up to 1 month. Scale any of these recipes linearly if you need a larger batch — the ratios above hold regardless of final volume.
:::

## Fresh working solutions (1000X stocks)

Make fresh each time — do not store.

| Component | Final stock | Recipe |
|-----------|-------------|--------|
| 1 M Dithiothreitol (DTT) | 1000X | 0.15425 g in 1 mL cell culture grade water |
| 0.15 M spermine | 1000X | 0.03035 g in 1 mL cell culture grade water |
| 0.5 M spermidine | 1000X | 0.072625 g in 1 mL cell culture grade water |

Add spermine, spermidine, and Dithiothreitol (DTT) to all buffers below for a final 1X concentration, **except** the nuclei resuspension buffer (see warning below).

Add RNase inhibitor to all buffers below: 0.5 U/µL SUPERase•In™ RNase Inhibitor (SUPERase) + 0.5 U/µL RNasin® Ribonuclease Inhibitor (RNAsin) — 1 U/µL total. Both are referred to by their short names (SUPERase, RNAsin) throughout the rest of this document.

---

## Working solutions — scaled to sample count

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Math audit — how every volume is calculated

**CitraHB Complete** (10 mL aliquot per sample — used in Steps 2, 3, and 6):

$$V_{aliquot} = 10\;mL \times N_{samples} \times (1 + overage)$$

Additives (SUPERase, RNAsin, spermidine, spermine, DTT) scale linearly with $V_{aliquot}$; protease inhibitor tablets are whole units, so the tablet count rounds up.

**Iodixanol step gradient** — each of the three working solutions is made by diluting 50% iodixanol (itself made 5 parts OptiPrep : 1 part Diluent, since OptiPrep ships at 60% and $5/6 \times 60\% = 50\%$) down to the target percentage with CitraPrepHB, using $C_1V_1 = C_2V_2$:

$$V_{50\%\ stock\ needed} = V_{total} \times \frac{\%_{target}}{50\%} \qquad V_{diluent} = V_{total} - V_{50\%\ stock\ needed}$$

Per-sample total volumes (from the source calculation): 15 mL of 50% (kept as-is), 4 mL of 40%, and 7.5 mL of 30%. All three scale with $N_{samples} \times (1+overage)$.

Polyamine additives in each gradient solution scale as $V_{total}/1000$ (spermidine, spermine, DTT — 1000X). SUPERase and RNAsin scale as:

$$V_{stock} = \frac{C_{final}}{C_{stock}} \times V_{total}$$

This protocol targets $C_{final} = 0.5$ U/µL for **each** inhibitor (not 0.2 U/µL), assuming a $C_{stock} = 40$ U/µL stock — both are single-source-of-truth cells (`rnase_final`, `rnase_stock`) up top, so edit them there if your stock concentration differs.

<!-- TODO: in the source spreadsheet, SUPERase/RNAsin added to the retained 50% fraction are computed at half the rate of the 40%/30% fractions (divided by 2). That halving is preserved here exactly as given — confirm with JP whether this is intentional before scaling to large batches. -->

**Nuclei resuspension buffer** (30 mL aliquot per sample):

$$V_{buffer} = 30\;mL \times N_{samples} \times (1+overage)$$

Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA) scales as 1% w/v of $V_{buffer}$; SUPERase and RNAsin use the same $C_{final}/C_{stock} \times V_{buffer}$ formula above. No spermine, spermidine, or Dithiothreitol (DTT) — these interfere with downstream cDNA synthesis.
:::

### CitraHB Complete (10 mL aliquot/sample)

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
chb_vol         = 10 * scale
chb_tablets     = Math.ceil(chb_vol / 10)
chb_rnase_uL    = rnase_vol(chb_vol * 1000)   // total volume in µL

Inputs.table([
  {Component: "Protease inhibitor tablet",               "Per 10 mL (aliquot)": "1 whole tablet",                    "Total": `${chb_tablets} tablet(s)`},
  {Component: `SUPERase (${rnase_final} U/µL final)`,     "Per 10 mL (aliquot)": `${fmt(rnase_vol(10000))} µL`,       "Total (µL)": fmt(chb_rnase_uL)},
  {Component: `RNAsin (${rnase_final} U/µL final)`,       "Per 10 mL (aliquot)": `${fmt(rnase_vol(10000))} µL`,       "Total (µL)": fmt(chb_rnase_uL)},
  {Component: "Spermidine (1000X)",                       "Per 10 mL (aliquot)": "10 µL",                             "Total (µL)": fmt(10 * chb_vol / 10)},
  {Component: "Spermine (1000X)",                         "Per 10 mL (aliquot)": "10 µL",                             "Total (µL)": fmt(10 * chb_vol / 10)},
  {Component: "Dithiothreitol (DTT, 1000X)",                              "Per 10 mL (aliquot)": "10 µL",                             "Total (µL)": fmt(10 * chb_vol / 10)},
  {Component: "CitraHB stock",                            "Per 10 mL (aliquot)": "to volume",                         "Total (mL)": fmt(chb_vol)}
], {layout: "auto"})
```

### Iodixanol step gradient

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
v50 = 15  * scale
v40 = 4   * scale
v30 = 7.5 * scale

optiprep_50 = v50 * 5/6
diluent_50  = v50 * 1/6

stock50_for_40  = v40 * 40/50
citraprephb_40  = v40 - stock50_for_40

stock50_for_30  = v30 * 30/50
citraprephb_30  = v30 - stock50_for_30

md`**50% iodixanol — ${fmt(v50)} mL total**`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Inputs.table([
  {Component: "OptiPrep",   "Volume (mL)": fmt(optiprep_50)},
  {Component: "Diluent",    "Volume (mL)": fmt(diluent_50)},
  {Component: "Spermidine (1000X)", "Volume (mL)": fmt(v50/1000)},
  {Component: "Spermine (1000X)",   "Volume (mL)": fmt(v50/1000)},
  {Component: "Dithiothreitol (DTT, 1000X)",        "Volume (mL)": fmt(v50/1000)},
  {Component: `SUPERase (${rnase_final} U/µL final)`, "Volume (mL)": fmt(rnase_vol(v50) / 2)},
  {Component: `RNAsin (${rnase_final} U/µL final)`,   "Volume (mL)": fmt(rnase_vol(v50) / 2)}
], {layout: "auto"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
md`**40% iodixanol — ${fmt(v40)} mL total**`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Inputs.table([
  {Component: "50% iodixanol (above)", "Volume (mL)": fmt(stock50_for_40)},
  {Component: "CitraPrepHB",           "Volume (mL)": fmt(citraprephb_40)},
  {Component: "Spermidine (1000X)",    "Volume (mL)": fmt(v40/1000)},
  {Component: "Spermine (1000X)",      "Volume (mL)": fmt(v40/1000)},
  {Component: "Dithiothreitol (DTT, 1000X)",           "Volume (mL)": fmt(v40/1000)},
  {Component: `SUPERase (${rnase_final} U/µL final)`, "Volume (mL)": fmt(rnase_vol(v40))},
  {Component: `RNAsin (${rnase_final} U/µL final)`,   "Volume (mL)": fmt(rnase_vol(v40))}
], {layout: "auto"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
md`**30% iodixanol — ${fmt(v30)} mL total**`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Inputs.table([
  {Component: "50% iodixanol (above)", "Volume (mL)": fmt(stock50_for_30)},
  {Component: "CitraPrepHB",           "Volume (mL)": fmt(citraprephb_30)},
  {Component: "Spermidine (1000X)",    "Volume (mL)": fmt(v30/1000)},
  {Component: "Spermine (1000X)",      "Volume (mL)": fmt(v30/1000)},
  {Component: "Dithiothreitol (DTT, 1000X)",           "Volume (mL)": fmt(v30/1000)},
  {Component: `SUPERase (${rnase_final} U/µL final)`, "Volume (mL)": fmt(rnase_vol(v30))},
  {Component: `RNAsin (${rnase_final} U/µL final)`,   "Volume (mL)": fmt(rnase_vol(v30))}
], {layout: "auto"})
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Add polyamines/RNase inhibitor last
Per the source protocol: make the base 50% iodixanol solution (OptiPrep + Diluent only) first, pull off the volumes you need to dilute into 40% and 30%, and only then add spermidine, spermine, DTT, SUPERase, and RNAsin to what remains.
:::

### Nuclei resuspension buffer (30 mL aliquot/sample)

::: {.callout-warning}
## No spermine, spermidine, or DTT in this buffer
These will interfere with downstream cDNA synthesis. Make this buffer during the Step 8 centrifugation spin.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
nrb_vol   = 30 * scale
nrb_bsa_g = nrb_vol * 1/100

Inputs.table([
  {Component: "Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA)",             "Amount": `${fmt(nrb_bsa_g)} g`},
  {Component: "1X Phosphate-Buffered Saline (PBS)",     "Amount": `to ${fmt(nrb_vol)} mL`},
  {Component: `SUPERase (${rnase_final} U/µL final)`,    "Amount": `${fmt(rnase_vol(nrb_vol))} mL`},
  {Component: `RNAsin (${rnase_final} U/µL final)`,      "Amount": `${fmt(rnase_vol(nrb_vol))} mL`}
], {layout: "auto"})
```

## Protocol

### Tissue homogenization (~30 min)

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Check nuclei before proceeding
Step 4 calls for pulling an aliquot to check nuclei release after homogenization — add more strokes with the tight pestle if intact cells are still visible before moving on.
:::

| Step | Action | Volume |
|------|--------|--------|
| 1 | Pre-chill 7 mL glass dounce homogenizer on ice | — |
| 2 | Cut snap-frozen tissue into small pieces (<0.5 cm) with clean scissors, in a petri dish on ice, in CitraHB complete | 1 mL/sample |
| 3 | Transfer to dounce homogenizer on ice; add CitraHB complete; incubate 7 min on ice | 4 mL/sample |
| 4 | Homogenize 20× with loose pestle; add Detergent; homogenize 20× with tight pestle. Pull an aliquot to check nuclei; homogenize further if needed | 320 µL/sample Detergent |
| 5 | Filter through 40 µM strainer | — |

### Iodixanol gradient centrifugation (~1 hr + spin)

::: {.callout-warning}
## No brake on the Step 8 spin
This spin is run on an **ultracentrifuge**: **18 min at 10,000×g at 4°C with no brake**. Braking will disturb the gradient interface and mix layers together, ruining nuclei recovery. Schedule the ultracentrifuge for **18 min** run time, but budget closer to **an hour** for the step overall — loading/vacuum draw-down, acceleration, and the unbraked coast to a stop add substantial time beyond the programmed 18 min.
:::

| Step | Action | Volume |
|------|--------|--------|
| 6 | Add 50% iodixanol solution to the filtered sample (5 mL CitraHB fraction) and vortex to mix | 5 mL/sample |
| 7 | Underlay sample with 30% and then 40% iodixanol solutions | Per gradient volumes above |
| 8 | Weigh conical tubes against each other on a scale, topping up the lighter tube(s) with cell culture grade water dropwise until matched (within ~0.1 g), then place balanced tubes opposite each other in the rotor; centrifuge in the ultracentrifuge for 18 min at 10,000×g, 4°C, **no brake** | — |
| 9 | Collect nuclei from the interface layer with a P1000 pipette; transfer to a new tube | — |

::: {.callout-important}
## Checklist
- [ ] Gradient tubes weighed against each other and balanced to within ~0.1 g before spinning
- [ ] Balanced tubes loaded opposite each other in the rotor
- [ ] Ultracentrifuge confirmed at no-brake setting
- [ ] Interface layer collected cleanly, minimal carryover of gradient layers
:::

### Nuclei wash & counting (~30 min)

| Step | Action | Volume |
|------|--------|--------|
| 10 | Add nuclei wash buffer in a 15 mL tube; vortex | 10 mL/sample |
| 11 | Filter through 20 µM filter | — |
| 12 | Spin 10 min at 500×g, 4°C to pellet nuclei | — |
| 13 | Resuspend in nuclei wash buffer; repeat spin (Step 12) | 10 mL/sample |
| 14 | Resuspend in nuclei wash buffer; count using hemocytometer (see method below) | 200 µL/sample |
| 15 | Load for single cell | — |

::: {.callout-tip}
## Hemocytometer counting method
CitraPrep nuclei yields are typically too low for a reliable Countess (automated) read, so this is a **manual hemocytometer count** every time — do not substitute the Countess.

a. Filter your trypan blue stock through a 0.2 µm filter before use — unfiltered trypan blue carries particulates that get miscounted as nuclei, and this matters more at low nuclei numbers where a few false counts skew the result.
b. Mix the nuclei suspension with filtered trypan blue at a **1:1** ratio (e.g. 10 µL suspension + 10 µL trypan blue) — dilution factor = 2.
c. Load 10 µL of the mix onto the hemocytometer; let it wick in by capillary action, no bubbles.
d. Under the microscope, count nuclei in the 4 corner grid squares (16 small squares each). Use the standard hemocytometer counting rule: count nuclei touching the top and left borders of a square, but not the bottom or right, to avoid double-counting nuclei that sit on a line.
e. Calculate concentration:

$$Nuclei/mL = \frac{\text{sum of nuclei in 4 corner squares}}{4} \times 2\ (\text{dilution factor}) \times 10^4$$

Divide by 1000 to convert to nuclei/µL for loading calculations.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## Checklist
- [ ] Trypan blue filtered (0.2 µm) before use
- [ ] Nuclei suspension diluted 1:1 with trypan blue
- [ ] Nuclei intact and free of debris under the hemocytometer
- [ ] Nuclei concentration: _______ nuclei/µL
- [ ] Loaded for single-cell run at: _______
:::
